When a server fails Incus marks it offline after about 20 seconds. Stateless replicas are replaced on other servers after a delay. Use this page when a majority of the cluster's database members is down. Incus keeps its cluster state in a replicated database. Members with the database role vote, and a majority of them must be reachable. Losing the majority (two of three voters) stops every change to the cluster; the instances keep running.

What you see Instances keep running and serving. Service addresses (OVN load balancers) keep forwarding. Apelora reports Incus as unavailable instead of guessing: API calls that read Incus fail with HTTP 502 ( incus_api_error "context deadline exceeded" after about 5 s, or incus_unreachable after about 20 s). The deploy identity ( APELORA_INCUS_CLIENT_CERT / KEY ) is restricted to the deploy projects and used by the control plane (inventory, preflight) and the deployment worker. The admin identity ( APELORA_INCUS_ADMIN_CLIENT_CERT / KEY ) is unrestricted, optional, and loaded only by the control plane ; the worker never receives it. t: ADR 0003 — Two Incus identities; members join with single-use tokens
x: Consequences A leaked deploy certificate cannot add members, change cluster configuration or touch other projects. The admin certificate is as sensitive as Incus itself and belongs in the control plane's secret store only. Cluster administration bypasses the job queue, so it has no retries or idempotency keys; failures are reported to the caller directly. Operations that need the admin identity are easy to find: they go through AppState.admin .

t: ADR 0003 — Two Incus identities; members join with single-use tokens
x: Alternatives One unrestricted identity for everything — simpler, but the worker (the component that runs most often and talks to Incus most) would hold full cluster control. Queue token creation as a job and store the token encrypted — adds key management for a secret that is needed exactly once, by the person who just asked for it. Apelora joins servers itself over SSH — Apelora would need credentials for every new host; the host-side join keeps that trust on the host.
